question.problem: Consider the function $g(x,y)={y}^{x}.$ What is the rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $(1,e)$ in the direction of the vector $v=⟨4,-3⟩?$
question.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $(1,e)$ in the direction of $v$ is equal to the directional derivative ${g}_{u}^{′}(1,e).$ 

First, we find the unit vector $u$ in the direction of $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{{4}^{2}+(-3)^{2}}=5 \\ u & =\frac{1}{5}⟨4,-3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the gradient $∇g(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,e):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇g(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}({y}^{x}),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}({y}^{x})⟩ \\  & =⟨{y}^{x}\operatorname{ln}⁡y,\,x{y}^{x-1}⟩ \\ ∇g(1,e) & =⟨{e}^{1}\operatorname{ln}⁡e,1{e}^{1-1}⟩ \\  & =⟨e,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the directional derivative ${g}_{u}^{′}(1,e)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{u}^{′}(1,e) & =∇g(1,e)\cdot u \\  & =⟨e,1⟩\cdot \frac{1}{5}⟨4,-3⟩ \\  & =\frac{e(4)+1(-3)}{5} \\  & =\frac{4e-3}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
